answer: A newcomer earns standing by sailing to an island at dawn to recite a sonnet naming its three tide markers — voice recording, tide reading, and timestamp, witnessed by a fellow traveller. Two island keepers verify the recording within five days, checking the lines against the sonnet ledger and the tide against the tide table. A copied sonnet, a recital at the wrong tide, or a missing marker voids the season, burns the 60-credit stake, and bars the sponsor a year. One honest season costs 60 credits; a thousand fakes need 1,000 dawn sailings and 1,000 sonnets, each checked against a real tide.
